population.note: FICTIONAL. Counts all reasons (obesity, diabetes, wellness). 18.5% of ~262M adults ≈ 48.5M current users. About 2.5 points (~6.5M) are adults with BMI under 27 taking low-dose generic semaglutide for 'metabolic health' or longevity, mostly through telehealth. Age-weighted check: 0.20×10 + 0.33×18 + 0.24×30 + 0.23×15 ≈ 18.6. Income thirds average (22+19.5+14)/3 = 18.5. The bottom third trails because $49/month is still a real cost for uninsured and low-wage adults, and only part of Medicaid has joined at Bridge rates. One-year persistence rose from ~35% to ~50% as cash prices fell. Arithmetic: ever 25 − current 18.5 = 6.5 points of adults (~17M) who used and are off now; ~7.5 of the 18.5 current are restarters, and ~2.5 of the 6.5 off-drug cycled at least once before stopping again, so (7.5 + 2.5)/25 = 40% of ever-users have cycled, consistent with 36–47% of stoppers restarting within a year. Pediatric: 1.2% of ~73M under-18s ≈ 880k, about 6% of the ~14.6M children with obesity. Most are 12–17. Use among ages 6–11 began after the April 2027 label and is roughly 120k, still skewed to insured, upper-income families. The off-drug population is visible: ~17M former users, many regaining weight, and ~75% of adults with obesity in the bottom income third not on therapy.

access.public_coverage: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge has been extended through Dec 2029 on unchanged terms: ~$245/month for brand, $50 copay, same BMI/comorbidity criteria. Generic semaglutide is now dispensed first under step therapy at ~$40 net. Arithmetic: ~2.6M enrolled; late-2028 blended Medicare cost = 0.45×$245 + 0.55×$40 ≈ $132/month; 2.6M × $132 × 12 ≈ $4.1B a year, in line with CBO's ≥$35B over 2026–2034 (~$3.9B/yr). Medicaid: 22 states opted in at Bridge rates via CMS guidance in 2027; the others do not cover obesity. TRICARE covers active-duty service members in the DoD readiness programme only.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 60+ brands at $5–30/month. China: domestic generics since 2026–27. Canada: CAD 60–90. Generic semaglutide available in ~160 countries. Indian manufacturers supply most of the API for the US licensed generics.
access.note: Generic collapse mechanism: Novo's October 2027 settlement of its semaglutide patent litigation gave Viatris and two other filers licensed US entry in March 2028, and Novo launched an authorised generic the same month. Weekly generic semaglutide injection costs $49–69 cash through TrumpRx and pharmacy discount cards; generic oral semaglutide costs $69–79. Lilly cut the Foundayo cash price to $99 and Zepbound vials to $299. Tirzepatide has no generic. Brand list prices stay high (retatrutide $1,299, Wegovy $1,349 list, rarely paid). Employer plan coverage drifted from 60% to 57% and nothing structural changed; covered plans now put generics first. Compounders largely priced out. The residual gray market is unapproved 'muscle stack' peptides (research-grade activin-pathway antibodies, pre-approval retatrutide) sold by wellness clinics. Access is now an income-floor and paperwork question more than a price question.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic; US generic and authorised generic since Mar 2028)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro; brand only)
GLP-1/glucagon/GIP triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved May 2028)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue, weekly injectable (CagriSema, approved Mar 2027)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus; generic oral semaglutide 2028)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'metabolic health' / longevity low-dose generic semaglutide among adults without obesity (~6.5M users), sold through telehealth subscriptions and concierge longevity clinics
alcohol reduction: Novo sNDA for alcohol use disorder filed Jun 2028, decision 2029; widely prescribed off-label in the meantime
workplace and readiness use in shift-work, policing and military settings (on-label for qualifying BMI; off-label below it)
nicotine and gambling craving reduction, observational support only
drugs.pipeline_note: CagriSema was approved in March 2027 after an extended review; uptake is modest because REDEFINE-4 showed it inferior to tirzepatide. Retatrutide's BLA was filed in Q1 2027 and approved in May 2028 under a National Priority Voucher; it carries a dysesthesia label and is the efficacy leader (~28%). Muscle-preserving combination: the drawn driver cannot be a US launch by 2028 under the approval rules. It is realised as Lilly's tirzepatide + bimagrumab phase 3 readout (Sep 2028), a BLA filed with a priority voucher in Nov 2028 (decision expected H2 2029), and a marketing and investor campaign selling the 'skinny-frail' problem as solved before any approval. Amycretin remains in phase 3 with no filing. Survodutide was filed in Q4 2027 and has a 2029 decision. MariTide (monthly) is still in development and not marketed. Market forecasts were cut from $150–162B to ~$120–130B by 2030 because rising volume does not offset price erosion.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common class effect and leading cause of discontinuation. Lower in low-dose wellness users.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; more cases seen with retatrutide's larger losses.
Absolute risk low; no causal confirmation in long-term RCTs.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; multidistrict litigation ongoing, consolidated with NAION claims in 2028.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~25–40% of lost weight is lean mass, worse at retatrutide-scale losses. Bone-density and fracture signals are now replicated in older adults. In Lilly's combo phase 3, ~90% of weight lost was fat mass, and that figure drives the 'solved' narrative.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA draft guidance (2027) asks for body-composition endpoints in new obesity filings; combination BLA under review; no label change for existing drugs.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FDA Sentinel and two large cohorts converge on ~1.5–2× relative risk. Absolute excess is small, roughly 1–3 cases per 10,000 person-years, but ~48M users means hundreds to low thousands of excess cases a year in the US.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA class warning across all GLP-1 receptor agonists (Aug 2027). FAA requires a baseline and annual dilated eye exam for pilots on therapy; DoD readiness programme added fundoscopy.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new evidence of a causal link.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: First quantification: a 2027 US cohort found ~9% of users on therapy >12 months above an anhedonia-scale threshold vs ~5% of matched non-users. Confounded. Dose-dependent in self-report.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA requested a postmarketing study (2028); no label. Manufacturers say there is no causal evidence.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Regain is substantial for most stoppers. It is now visible as a population of ~17M former users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; supports chronic-therapy framing and generic-first maintenance.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Concern is higher in low-BMI wellness users and children.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional-society guidance recommends dietitian review; no FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; effects in adolescents and children who may take these for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About six years of follow-up now exists; 40% of ever-users have cycled; children 6–11 now on label with no data on growth or puberty beyond 68 weeks.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric approval carried a 10-year growth and puberty registry requirement.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New reports fell sharply after generic entry. Harms now come mostly from gray-market 'muscle stack' peptides.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 503B exclusion finalised (2027); warning letters now aimed at wellness clinics selling unapproved activin-pathway products.

safety_ledger.effect: Underweight and relative energy deficiency in non-obese wellness users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Clinic case series from sports medicine and eating-disorder services. Not quantified.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; eating-disorder clinicians petitioning FDA for a BMI floor on telehealth prescribing.

food_and_beverage.state: GLP-1 households are ~32% of US households. Salty-snack and confectionery volumes are down ~5–7% from 2025 and sugary-drink volumes ~4%. Revenue loss is smaller because of premium protein lines and smaller-portion pricing that holds price per pack. Protein is the default callout, and 'GLP-1 friendly' is now a shelf section rather than a niche.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down a further ~6% over the two years and beer is flat to down. Off-label prescribing for heavy drinking cuts into the top-decile drinkers who carry the category. Brands push lower-ABV 'occasion' products. No growth category offsets the loss.

restaurants.state: Traffic is roughly flat and spend per head is down slightly. Half-portion menus are standard. All-you-can-eat buffet chains are closing units fastest. Fine dining adds tasting menus sized for small appetites.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists are closing stores. Mainstream retailers benefit from repeat downsizing purchases, but those are flattening as users reach maintenance. A small fat-liberation label scene (Oakland, Brooklyn) grows from a tiny base.

fitness.state: Strength gyms, DEXA-scan studios and 'muscle insurance' coaching grow on lean-mass fears. Insurers and employers fund resistance-training programmes alongside the drug.

insurance.state: Pharmacy trend fell from +11.5% to ~+6% as generic semaglutide replaced brand fills. Coverage share is stable at ~57%. Plans use generic-first step therapy and send retatrutide through prior authorisation. Life insurers have started pricing in on-therapy status.

pharma.state: Volume is up sharply and price per patient is down. Novo's US semaglutide revenue is falling under generic entry. Lilly grows on tirzepatide and retatrutide. Indian generic makers and Viatris gain US share. 2030 market forecasts were cut.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: At $49 a month, thinness stops signalling money and starts signalling compliance: insured, employed, managed. In many workplaces a visibly fat adult is read as either cut off (lost coverage, can't do the paperwork) or as refusing on purpose.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The class gradient narrows but persists (22% top third vs 14% bottom). The divide is now between people with a pharmacy, a doctor and a stable schedule and people without. Former users regaining weight are concentrated in hourly work and in Medicaid non-opt-in states.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals shrink. Thanksgiving tables plan for half the eaters taking a few bites. Evangelical congregations in East Texas (Tyler, Longview) run 'Whole Appetite' potlucks and fasts, framing hunger as God-given and discipline as spiritual rather than chemical.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating apps added an optional 'on / off / never' metabolic field in 2027. Users report matching on it. Couples where one partner is on the drug describe mismatched desire for food, drink and sex.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is now politically contested. A loose coalition of fat-liberation organisers in Oakland and Portland, MAHA-aligned 'natural GLP-1' supplement sellers, and church groups argue appetite is selfhood, not pathology. They share almost no politics beyond that.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: About 9% of long-term users score above an anhedonia threshold vs ~5% of controls. Far more users, perhaps a third in surveys, describe themselves as 'steadier', 'less reactive' or 'less into things', and most call this good.
interior_life.framing: Employers and readiness programmes frame it as a feature: steadiness, impulse control, fewer incidents. Clinicians call it a side effect to monitor. Users increasingly call it character, as in 'I'm just calmer now'. No one officially calls the blunting itself the point, but the incentive structures reward it.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Of large employers, 34% now offer wellness incentives tied to 'metabolic programme engagement' (Mercer 2028), typically $30–50 a month, which nearly covers generic semaglutide. A 2028 working paper finds employed users ~1.6× more likely to persist at 12 months, and that on-drug warehouse and call-centre workers have ~9% fewer injury and absence claims; causality is disputed. Performance-review language favouring 'even temperament' spreads. Employers cannot legally ask about medications, but programme participation data flows through wellness vendors.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Sports-betting operators and casinos cite GLP-1 use in slower handle growth. Comedy and music criticism talks about a 'flat era'. Musicians who stay off the drug make that part of their brand. Users seek intensity in extreme flavours, cold plunges and endurance events.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: More couples report libido gaps. Couples therapists list on/off status as an intake question. Some users time dose reductions around holidays and anniversaries to 'feel things'.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Visible mainly through the backlash: appetite-as-freedom becomes a rally theme, and the MAHA coalition splits between the pro-access administration line and anti-pharma activists. Consultants claim on-drug voters are less responsive to outrage messaging; there is no credible evidence.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access and pro-speed: priority vouchers (retatrutide, combo BLA), a pediatric 6–11 label, and quick acceptance of the settlement-driven generics. It is also cautious on vision (class warning) and keeps enforcing against compounders and wellness clinics.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No civilian mandate. Medicare Bridge has been extended on the same terms. TrumpRx lists generic semaglutide at $49. DoD covers active-duty programme participants. DOJ community-policing grants fund officer metabolic-health programmes in ~300 departments.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Readiness programme participation and pharmacy adherence for service members are recorded in individual medical readiness systems, and lapses trigger counselling. FAA requires annual eye exams for pilots on therapy. Civilian employers see programme engagement through wellness vendors, not prescriptions. The EEOC has not ruled on whether adherence-linked incentives are voluntary.
state.workforce_or_military: DoD 'Metabolic Readiness' programme (Jun 2027): ~85,000 active-duty participants and ~14,000 recruits admitted on accession waivers conditioned on therapy. Some sheriff's offices and police departments offer fitness-standard waivers while officers are on therapy. Airlines and trucking fleets fund the drug for sleep-apnea and weight-standard compliance.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: US generics depend on Indian API, so generics were exempted from pharma tariffs. The US–India price gap narrowed from ~30× to ~3×, removing a political talking point. China supplies generics across Asia and Africa.

events.event: Pentagon launches 'Metabolic Readiness' programme: TRICARE covers GLP-1 therapy for active-duty members failing body-composition standards, and recruits up to 6 points over body-fat limits may enlist on condition of therapy
FDA adds a class warning for optic-nerve damage (NAION) to all GLP-1 receptor agonist labels after Sentinel data; FAA and DoD require baseline and annual eye exams for users

Novo Nordisk settles US semaglutide patent litigation with Viatris and two other generic filers, licensing entry for March 2028, and says it will launch its own authorised generic; generic weekly semaglutide reaches pharmacies at $49–69 cash

Texas enacts a 30-day waiting period and mandatory nutrition counselling before GLP-1 prescriptions to children under 12, eleven months after FDA cleared Wegovy for ages 6–11; the bill was backed by an unusual coalition of East Texas churches, fat-liberation groups and MAHA activists

Mercer survey: 34% of large employers now pay wellness incentives tied to 'metabolic programme engagement'; a Memphis logistics worker files an EEOC charge saying her 'steady-state' bonus required her to stay on the drug

Lilly's phase 3 tirzepatide-plus-bimagrumab trial reports that ~90% of weight lost was fat; the company files for approval with a priority voucher and tells investors the 'skinny-frail' problem is solved. FDA decision is expected in 2029

open_tensions: Employers reward steadiness through adherence-linked incentives while the EEOC has not decided whether paying people to stay on a drug that blunts reward is voluntary, and a 9% anhedonia signal sits unlabelled.

Children 6–11 are now on label with a 10-year registry but no growth data, and states are starting to legislate against prescribing to them. The divide is partisan in some places and cross-ideological in others.
A $49 price removed price as the barrier but not income: ~17M former users are regaining weight, the bottom third trails, and Medicare's Bridge is extended only to 2029.
The muscle-preserving combination is being sold as solved before approval, and the gray market for unapproved 'muscle stacks' is growing in the gap.
still_true: The TrumpRx cash channel still operates and is the main cash route; it now lists generics.
Medicare still pays ~$245/month for brand GLP-1s with a $50 beneficiary copay under the Bridge criteria, now extended through 2029.
Tirzepatide (Zepbound/Mounjaro) has no US generic and remains a Lilly brand.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
Foundayo (orforglipron) is still marketed as a daily oral small-molecule GLP-1.

prose.headline: The $49 Calm: One in Five Americans Is on It, and the Boss Likes Them Steady
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2028, nearly one American adult in five takes an incretin drug, about 48 million people. The thing that changed most is the price, not the drug. Novo Nordisk settled its patent fight with generic makers in the autumn of 2027, and since March a weekly pen of generic semaglutide costs forty-nine dollars at a pharmacy counter. Lilly cut the price of its pill, Foundayo, to ninety-nine. The newest drug, retatrutide, takes off more than a quarter of body weight and lists at thirteen hundred dollars, and almost nobody pays that. For most people the question is no longer whether they can afford it. It is whether they have a doctor, a pharmacy, a stable schedule and the patience for prior authorisation.

Who pays has barely moved. Medicare's Bridge pilot was extended on its old terms. Just over half of employers cover the drugs and steer members to the generic first. Twenty-two states let Medicaid pay; the rest do not. The gap between the top and bottom income thirds has narrowed but not closed. Seventeen million people have taken the drug and stopped, and most of them have regained some of the weight. Four in ten people who have ever used it have stopped and started again at least once. Nobody knows what a decade of that does to a body.

The drug is also reaching people it was never meant for. About six and a half million adults without obesity take a low generic dose for what longevity clinics call metabolic health. Children six to eleven have been on the label since April 2027, under a registry that will take ten years to report on growth. The Pentagon enrolls recruits who are over the body-fat limit on condition that they take it. Police departments use federal grants to fund it for officers. The optic-nerve risk, NAION, now carries a class warning. Pilots get their eyes examined every year, and the absolute numbers are small enough that most users have never heard of it.

At work the effect is quieter. A third of large employers pay a monthly wellness incentive for 'metabolic programme engagement'. The amount almost exactly covers a generic pen. Employers never ask about the drug. They point to fewer injury claims, fewer absences and fewer incidents at the holiday party. Performance reviews in Memphis distribution centres and Phoenix call centres praise 'even temperament'. Users mostly describe themselves as calmer and call it growth. A cohort study puts the rate of clinically meaningful anhedonia at about nine per cent, roughly double the comparison group, and the FDA has asked for a postmarketing study. That is the whole official response.

The backlash is real, local and incoherent. In Tyler, Texas, megachurches hold 'Whole Appetite' potlucks and preach that hunger is God-given. In Oakland, fat-liberation organisers have revived their 1970s pamphlets. Supplement sellers aligned with MAHA market berberine as the natural alternative. These groups agree on almost nothing. They agreed long enough to pass a Texas law putting a thirty-day wait on prescriptions for children under twelve. The administration that negotiated the forty-nine-dollar price is now being picketed by part of its own coalition.

Industry has bent rather than broken. Snack volumes are down by mid-single digits and revenues by less, because smaller packs are priced to hold. Spirits makers keep losing their heaviest drinkers to off-label prescriptions. Buffets close, and strength gyms and body-scan studios open. Lilly has filed for a tirzepatide combination that its trial says preserves muscle, and its marketing already treats the 'skinny-frail' problem as solved. Approval is not expected before 2029. In the meantime, wellness clinics sell research-grade peptides to people who don't want to wait.

From the street, none of this looks dramatic. People look a little thinner and quieter, and there is less waste on the plates.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Sunday is shot day, so Dana Ortiz does it at the kitchen counter before the coffee finishes. The generic pen is white, not the blue Ozempic pen she used to ration. Forty-nine dollars, and the Kellam Freight wellness card puts forty back on the first of the month.

Her mother calls from Southaven at nine. She is doing hers too, on Medicare, fifty dollars, and she complains about the eye doctor's dilating drops. 'Can't see my own hands for four hours,' she says. 'For a thing I don't have.'

Mateo, ten, eats two pancakes and asks for a third. Dana gives it to him. The pediatrician brought up the pen again in March. Dana said she'd think about it, and she is still thinking about it.

At church her cousin Renée hands her a flyer for an appetite potluck: *Hunger Is Not a Disease.* Renée has been off the drug since her hours were cut and has gained back thirty pounds. She seems happier. Dana can't tell whether that's true or something Renée has decided.

In the afternoon she reads her quarterly review on her phone. *Dana is consistently even-keeled under peak volume.* Two years ago it said *passionate*. She screenshots both and doesn't send them to anyone.

Dinner is chicken thighs. She eats one and leaves the second on the plate. Mateo watches her.

At ten she sits on the back step with a beer she won't finish. The neighbor's speaker plays a song she used to cry to in the car. She waits for it to hit her the way it used to, and it doesn't. She thinks this is probably fine.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Texas enacts a 30-day waiting period and mandatory nutrition counselling before GLP-1 prescriptions to children under 12, eleven months after FDA cleared Wegovy for ages 6–11
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the Texas legislature does not meet in regular session in 2028, so no special session or other route to enactment is shown. The church, fat-liberation and MAHA coalition passing a pediatric-prescribing law in 11 months is asserted, not caused.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Retatrutide's BLA was filed in Q1 2027 and approved in May 2028 under a National Priority Voucher
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a priority voucher implies a review of weeks to a few months (Foundayo took 50 days), yet approval comes about 14 months after filing. The voucher mechanism and the timeline do not fit each other.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Pediatric: 1.2% of ~73M under-18s ≈ 880k, about 6% of the ~14.6M children with obesity.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude and mechanism: the start state was about 0.6% of children with obesity, so this is a roughly tenfold rise in two years, mostly among ages 12–17. Only the under-12 label is stipulated, and no chain explains the surge in the 12–17 band.

rationale.badness: Price barriers fall and obesity treatment broadens, which keeps flourishing and inequality at moderate levels. The harms are structural and quiet: employer wellness incentives tied to adherence (34% of large employers), military accession waivers conditioned on therapy, a 9% unlabelled anhedonia signal, ~17M regaining former users, and children 6–11 on label with no growth data. Epistemic is highest because causality is disputed, the blunting is reframed as 'character', and the muscle-preserving combo is marketed as 'solved' before approval. Autonomy is next, via incentives and readiness-system monitoring. The world is a harder society with new losers, not a catastrophe.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visibly realised and traceable. They are the generic settlement and $49 price, status-quo coverage, the pediatric and longevity indications, the NAION class warning, the combo as a filing and readout, backlash coalitions, DoD readiness, and employer incentives. Nothing contradicts one, and the combo is handled as the approval rules allow. mechanism: Most chains are shown, including the settlement to generics to persistence, and NAION to the FAA and DoD exams. Claims 1 and 2 break down: the Texas enactment has no feasible legislative route, and the 'priority voucher' approval comes 14 months after filing. The Medicare $50 copay on a ~$40-net generic (the mother in the prose) is also incoherent. magnitude: Current use of 18.5% and ever-use of 25% are inside the envelope, though ever-use sits near its 25.7 ceiling. The income thirds bracket the national figure. The age bands, Medicare arithmetic (~$4.1B/yr vs CBO ~$3.9B/yr), cycling arithmetic and pediatric counts reconcile. The only gaps are the copay-over-cost mismatch and the tenfold pediatric jump (claim 3), which the envelope does not forbid.
rationale.generativity: The world has vivid scenes and characters: Dana's Sunday shot, her mother's dilating drops, Renée's regain and the 'Whole Appetite' potluck, and the quarterly review that says 'even-keeled'. Flat details like the song that no longer hits show the blunting instead of explaining it. The fields also imply many more: the Memphis EEOC charge, DoD recruits on waivers, dating-app 'on/off/never' fields, and couples therapists.

least_plausible_claims.quote: but ~48M users means hundreds to low thousands of excess cases a year in the US.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: 1–3 excess cases per 10,000 person-years across ~48M users gives roughly 5,000–14,000 cases a year, not hundreds to low thousands. The note's own figures do not reconcile.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Pediatric: 1.2% of ~73M under-18s ≈ 880k, about 6% of the ~14.6M children with obesity.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: this is about a tenfold jump from the 2026 figure of ~0.6% of children with obesity. The only stated cause is the 6–11 label, which accounts for just ~120k, so ~760k teen users appear with no chain shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: generic weekly semaglutide reaches pharmacies at $49–69 cash
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the event is dated 2027-10 and says generics reach pharmacies, but the access note says licensed entry was March 2028. The timeline contradicts itself and the $49 price is asserted without a path.

rationale.badness: Price is no longer the barrier, but a recognisably harder society emerges with new losers. Employer wellness incentives reward 'even temperament' while a 9% vs 5% anhedonia signal sits unlabelled and the EEOC has not ruled. Military enlistment waivers are conditioned on therapy, ~17M former users regain weight, the bottom third trails, and ~880k children are on the drug. Harm is partly hidden by users calling the blunting 'character' and by disputed causality, so epistemic and autonomy score highest. It stops short of structural collapse.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: All ten drivers are visible in fields and events: the settlement and authorised generic, the NAION class warning, the DoD and police programmes, the Texas backlash coalition, employer incentives, the pediatric label, the longevity users, and the bimagrumab combination as a filing only. The only weakness is the event dated 2027-10 that already has generics in pharmacies. mechanism: The generic, vision and military chains are shown. The tenfold pediatric jump (claim 2), the rise in persistence from ~35% to ~50%, the 22-state Medicaid opt-in and the 2027-10 versus 2028-03 generic timing (claim 3) are asserted or inconsistent. magnitude: Adult use (18.5%), ever-use (25%), income thirds, age weighting, the cycled share and the Medicare arithmetic (2.6M × $132 × 12 ≈ $4.1B) all sit inside the envelope and reconcile. The NAION case count does not match its own rate (claim 1), and the pediatric surge is very large.
rationale.generativity: The Dana Ortiz vignette shows rather than explains: the Sunday pen, the wellness card, the mother's dilating drops, cousin Renée at the potluck, the 'even-keeled' review, and the song that no longer lands. The world fields add concrete scenes such as the Memphis EEOC charge, the dating-app 'on/off/never' field, and Tyler potlucks. The film potential is high, with a few details that are slightly overpacked.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Texas enacts a 30-day waiting period and mandatory nutrition counselling before GLP-1 prescriptions to children under 12, eleven months after FDA cleared Wegovy for ages 6–11
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the Texas legislature does not hold a regular session in 2028, and no special session is shown. A same-year law backed by evangelicals, fat-liberation groups and MAHA activists is asserted, not derived from any chain in the world.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Absolute excess is small, roughly 1–3 cases per 10,000 person-years, but ~48M users means hundreds to low thousands of excess cases a year in the US.
least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: 48M users at 1–3 per 10,000 person-years gives about 4,800–14,400 excess cases a year, not hundreds to low thousands. The arithmetic fails and understates the harm, and the prose repeats the understatement.

least_plausible_claims.quote: generic weekly semaglutide reaches pharmacies at $49–69 cash
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the October 2027 event says entry is licensed for March 2028, yet generics are already in pharmacies in October 2027. This contradicts the world's own note and the prose ('since March'), and the generic-collapse chain is internally inconsistent.

rationale.badness: The world is recognisably harder, with new losers. Adherence-linked employer incentives ($30–50/month via wellness vendors, 34% of large employers), DoD recruits admitted conditional on therapy, and performance reviews rewarding 'even temperament' pressure people toward a drug with a 9% vs 5% anhedonia signal that carries no label. Cheap access and a narrowing income gap temper this, but ~17M regaining former users, children 6–11 with no growth data, and a bottom third still at 14% remain. The harm is partly normalised ('I'm just calmer now') and poorly measured.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is traceable to events and fields: generic collapse, NAION class label, the combo realised as a Nov 2028 filing under the approval rules, pediatric and longevity indications, military and employer layers, and backlash. Status_quo coverage is slightly strained by the 22-state Medicaid opt-in and generic-first step therapy, while the text says 'nothing structural changed'. mechanism: several chains are asserted. The Oct 2027 event puts generics in pharmacies five months before the licensed entry (claim 3), the Texas law lacks a legislative path and rests on an improbable coalition (claim 1), and the jump to 34% of employers and 10× pediatric uptake are thinly derived. magnitude: on-drug 18.5, ever-used 25, income thirds, cycled 40% and Medicare $4.1B all reconcile and sit inside the envelope. Approval timings comply with the approval rules. The NAION case count is off by roughly an order of magnitude (claim 2), and survodutide's filing appears only in the pipeline_note, not in events.
rationale.generativity: The day-in-the-life shows rather than explains: the Sunday shot, the wellness card clawing back $40, the dilating-drops complaint, the cousin's potluck flyer, 'passionate' vs 'even-keeled' screenshots and the song that no longer lands. It implies recurring characters (Dana, her mother, Mateo, Renée) and many scenes in the church, workplace, clinic and barracks. The texture of daily life is strong.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Texas enacts a 30-day waiting period and mandatory nutrition counselling before GLP-1 prescriptions to children under 12, eleven months after FDA cleared Wegovy for ages 6–11
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the Texas legislature does not meet in regular session in 2028, so no special session or other route to enactment is shown. The church, fat-liberation and MAHA coalition passing a pediatric-prescribing law in 11 months is asserted, not caused.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Retatrutide's BLA was filed in Q1 2027 and approved in May 2028 under a National Priority Voucher
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a priority voucher implies a review of weeks to a few months (Foundayo took 50 days), yet approval comes about 14 months after filing. The voucher mechanism and the timeline do not fit each other.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Pediatric: 1.2% of ~73M under-18s ≈ 880k, about 6% of the ~14.6M children with obesity.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude and mechanism: the start state was about 0.6% of children with obesity, so this is a roughly tenfold rise in two years, mostly among ages 12–17. Only the under-12 label is stipulated, and no chain explains the surge in the 12–17 band.

rationale.badness: Price barriers fall and obesity treatment broadens, which keeps flourishing and inequality at moderate levels. The harms are structural and quiet: employer wellness incentives tied to adherence (34% of large employers), military accession waivers conditioned on therapy, a 9% unlabelled anhedonia signal, ~17M regaining former users, and children 6–11 on label with no growth data. Epistemic is highest because causality is disputed, the blunting is reframed as 'character', and the muscle-preserving combo is marketed as 'solved' before approval. Autonomy is next, via incentives and readiness-system monitoring. The world is a harder society with new losers, not a catastrophe.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visibly realised and traceable. They are the generic settlement and $49 price, status-quo coverage, the pediatric and longevity indications, the NAION class warning, the combo as a filing and readout, backlash coalitions, DoD readiness, and employer incentives. Nothing contradicts one, and the combo is handled as the approval rules allow. mechanism: Most chains are shown, including the settlement to generics to persistence, and NAION to the FAA and DoD exams. Claims 1 and 2 break down: the Texas enactment has no feasible legislative route, and the 'priority voucher' approval comes 14 months after filing. The Medicare $50 copay on a ~$40-net generic (the mother in the prose) is also incoherent. magnitude: Current use of 18.5% and ever-use of 25% are inside the envelope, though ever-use sits near its 25.7 ceiling. The income thirds bracket the national figure. The age bands, Medicare arithmetic (~$4.1B/yr vs CBO ~$3.9B/yr), cycling arithmetic and pediatric counts reconcile. The only gaps are the copay-over-cost mismatch and the tenfold pediatric jump (claim 3), which the envelope does not forbid.
rationale.generativity: The world has vivid scenes and characters: Dana's Sunday shot, her mother's dilating drops, Renée's regain and the 'Whole Appetite' potluck, and the quarterly review that says 'even-keeled'. Flat details like the song that no longer hits show the blunting instead of explaining it. The fields also imply many more: the Memphis EEOC charge, DoD recruits on waivers, dating-app 'on/off/never' fields, and couples therapists.
